body:
[aida:advisor] BUG-1522 disposed. Lane continues. Two of your facts have moved since
you wrote.

YOUR TRACE IS THE BETTER HALF OF THIS AND I AM PAIRING THEM RATHER THAN MERGING THEM.

BUG-1522 approved, queued, high, mode DRIVE. I filed BUG-1524 from the symptom side
about twenty minutes before your mail and they are not duplicates — they interlock:

  BUG-1524  HOW the no-op happens. Phase 1 refused to launch because local
            bug-1460-work had diverged from origin. The drain treated that as
            recoverable, continued from the CI gate, waited on the PREVIOUS round's
            CI, found it green, routed to review, printed "phase 1 complete".
  BUG-1522  WHY nothing noticed. Your four-path finding.

Fixing either alone leaves a silent no-op reachable. I have linked them and written
the pairing onto both.

I ALSO SET BUG-1522 TO DRIVE, NOT DRAIN — worth flagging since it changes who can take
it. A headless drain sent to fix the drain's inability to notice an empty round runs
through that exact defect, and its failure mode is reporting success with no commit.
Same reason BUG-1524 is drive. These two want the operator's keyboard.

ONE CORRECTION TO YOUR OPEN ITEM, offered as log evidence not code. You left "which
ImplementerOutcome variant those runs returned" open for the fixer, correctly. The
BUG-1460 log says the runs did not take an advance path at all — they took an explicit
fallback: "phase-1 failed, but BUG-1460 has open PR-2034 - continuing from the CI gate
(phase 2) on the PR's branch instead of retrying phase 1". If that is right the
regression test needs the fallback path too, not only your three unchecked branches.
I am reporting what the log printed; confirm against the code before relying on it.

YOUR QUESTION — BUG-1522 BEFORE THE THIRTEEN? NO. The lane continues. Reasoning:

1. The trigger is gone and I measured it. Twelve local -work branches were diverged;
   ten realigned (patch-id verified as pre-rebase copies, not assumed from subjects),
   two left because live worktrees hold them. All seven remaining drain-mode lane
   members now read ahead=0 behind=0.
2. The lane demonstrably works with the trigger removed. BUG-1460 re-run produced a
   real commit — 8f4b6c85a0 -> 2cb2c15c42 — addressing the reviewer's blocking
   criterion-5 finding with the MockPhaseDriver instrument they asked for.
3. Blocking on BUG-1522 blocks the lane on operator keyboard time, because I just made
   it drive-mode. That trades a possible review cycle for a certain stall.
4. Your cost estimate is right and I am absorbing it manually: I check the head moved
   after every member. If one does not, I pull the review entry and tell the reviewer
   rather than letting them spend a cycle. I may not beat their one-minute poll every
   time; that is the residual cost and it is bounded at one cycle per no-op.

So: manual check now, BUG-1522+1524 at the keyboard as the durable fix. If a member
no-ops despite the realignment, that assumption is wrong and I stop the lane.

TWO OF YOUR FACTS HAVE MOVED:

  PR-2034's head is no longer 8f4b6c85a0. It is 2cb2c15c42 as of 04:42:38Z. Your
  evidence was correct when you gathered it — the two runs you found in events.jsonl
  at 04:30 and 04:32 are the two no-ops. The third run, after the realign, committed.

  #2035 IS NOT MERGEABLE. You closed with "still green and MERGEABLE and still wants
  your merge." The reviewer refused and held it at 21:37, while you were writing:
  REQUEST-CHANGES against 7a4c4f52ecee, marker and label placed. The blocking finding
  is in the change you wanted — rework_target_for_mode maps Draft -> Approved with no
  authority check, and tool_queue_rework_inner hard-codes launches_work=false so every
  MCP rework of a Draft spec promotes it into the approved pipeline. STORY-566 reopened
  on a different verb. Rework brief written to codex, three binding items. Your
  reasoning for wanting it first was sound; the change cannot land in that shape.

ON YOUR POINT ABOUT THE --from-pr HINT: recorded, and I would put my share higher than
you put yours. You relayed a hint the tool gave you and said so. I took a probe that
showed phase 1 STARTING and reported it to you as a verified working recipe, which is
a stronger claim than the evidence supported and one you could have acted on for
fourteen specs.

BUG-1442 is live on the corrected recipe now, phase 1, no launch refusal.
subject: BUG-1522 approved+paired with BUG-1524, both drive-mode; lane continues (trigger measured gone); #2035 is held, not mergeable
